title.value: ProtST: Multi-Modality Learning of Protein Sequences and Biomedical Texts
title.justification: The paper's title precisely reflects its focus on integrating protein sequences and biomedical texts through a multi-modality learning framework called ProtST.
title.quote: ProtST: Multi-Modality Learning of Protein Sequences and Biomedical Texts

extractions.description: This paper presents the ProtST framework, a novel approach to enhance protein sequence representation learning by integrating biomedical text descriptions. It introduces the ProtDescribe dataset, which pairs protein sequences with textual property descriptions and proposes multi-modal pre-training tasks to improve protein function prediction, enabling both supervised and zero-shot learning capabilities.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the bioinformatics and computational biology domain, specifically on protein sequence representation learning enhanced by biomedical texts. Although it might have implications for applications in healthcare and drug discovery, it does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our work aims to enhance protein sequence representation learning by using textual protein property descriptions.

applications.justification: The ProtST framework enhances protein function prediction through improved sequence representation, applicable in drug discovery and related fields.
applications.quote: ProtST enables both supervised learning and zero-shot prediction. We verify the superiority of ProtST-induced PLMs over previous ones on diverse representation learning benchmarks.
